title: [Bug]: An explicit plugin that cannot be fetched makes the first message return a raw 500, and the conversation cannot be fixed

labels.name: priority:medium
labels.description: For bugs, a serious source of annoyance, but not blocking a large number of users.

body:
_This issue was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of @neubig._ ## Summary A plugin attached explicitly to a conversation (`StartConversationRequest.plugins`) is fetched lazily, on the first message. If that fetch fails, `POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` returns a raw **HTTP 500** `{"detail": "Internal Server Error", ...}`. The error goes through the generic unhandled-exception handler. The client gets no status code or error code that it can act on. Explicit plugins failing closed is intended (see #6439: a requested plugin may carry policy hooks, so the conversation must not run without it). This issue does not change that. The problems are how the failure reaches the client and what the user can do next: 1. The status is always 500. The server does not separate "your plugin source is wrong" (fix the input) from "the git host failed" (retry later). The `/load_plugin` route already maps the same `PluginFetchError` to 400. The send route does not. 2. The `plugins` list cannot be changed after create. If the source is wrong (typo, wrong repo, deleted repo), every message to the conversation fails with 500 for good. 3. `POST /api/conversations` with an `initial_message` also returns 500, but the conversation is already persisted. The client does not get its id, so the conversation is orphaned. 4. Every failed send re-runs the auto-load marketplaces, so each retry adds one more `MarketplaceLoadError` event to the conversation. Related: #7100 (an auto-loaded marketplace that fails is never retried). That issue covers the auto-load path and the lost git error. This issue covers the explicit-attach path. Root cause 4 below is shared. ## Answers to the open questions - **Is the user message stored before the failure? No.** `send_message()` runs the lazy init before it creates the `MessageEvent`. So a resend does not make a duplicate. The repro shows 0 user messages after two failed sends and exactly 1 after the successful resend. (Exception: for `ACPAgent`, `send_message()` skips the init ([L2452-L2453](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L2452-L2453)), so the message is stored and the fetch fails later in `run()`. I found this by reading the code. I did not test it.) - **Can the user retry? Only if the same source starts to work.** `_plugins_loaded` is set only at the end of a successful load, so each send fetches again. The resend succeeds once the source is reachable, and the plugin's skills and hooks load. But no API can change the attached `plugins` (`UpdateConversationRequest` has only `title`, `tags` and `max_budget_per_run`). So the user cannot fix a wrong source. The one partial way out: `${VAR}` placeholders in the source are expanded from the conversation's secret registry on each attempt, so a bad credential could be fixed with `POST /{id}/secrets`. (I found this by reading the code. I did not test it.) - **Are retryable and permanent failures told apart? No.** Every git failure (missing repo, 404, 503, DNS, auth) becomes the same `Failed to fetch plugin from `, and the server answers 500 for all of them. A source string that cannot be parsed is not checked at create time either. It fails only on the first message. ## Root cause All links are at `15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d`. 1. **Explicit plugin failures are re-raised from the lazy init.** In `_ensure_plugins_loaded()`, an auto-loaded plugin that fails is skipped with a warning. An explicit one is re-raised ([local_conversation.py L1320-L1344](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L1320-L1344)): ```python except Exception as exc: # Attaching a plugin that cannot load is an error, but an # auto-loaded one must not prevent the conversation from starting. if not auto_loaded: raise ``` This runs inside `send_message()` → `_ensure_agent_ready()` ([L2452-L2453](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L2452-L2453), [L2056-L2057](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L2056-L2057)), before the `MessageEvent` is created ([L2493-L2500](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L2493-L2500)). `_plugins_loaded` is set only at [L1568](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L1568), so the next send tries again. 2. **The send route does not map the error.** `send_message` in the event router calls `event_service.send_message(...)` with no `except` ([event_router.py L319-L324](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_router.py#L319-L324)). `PluginFetchError` is a plain `Exception` ([fetch.py L28-L29](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/plugin/fetch.py#L28-L29)), not a `DomainError`. So it falls through to `_unhandled_exception_handler`, which answers 500 ([api.py L837-L898](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/api.py#L837-L898)). Compare `/load_plugin`, which maps the same error to `Invalid` (400) ([conversation_router.py L811-L823](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/conversation_router.py#L811-L823)). The WebSocket send path at least wraps it in a `ServerErrorEvent` with `code="PluginFetchError"` ([sockets.py L321-L336](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/sockets.py#L321-L336)). 3. **Create persists first, then sends the initial message.** `_launch_prepared_conversation` starts and persists the event service, then calls `send_message` outside the lifecycle lock. The exception is re-raised with no rollback ([conversation_service.py L1938-L1966](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/conversation_service.py#L1938-L1966)). 4. **The fetch layer drops the git error** (shared with #7100). `try_cached_clone_or_update` turns every `GitCommandError` into `None` ([cached_repo.py L910-L920](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/git/cached_repo.py#L910-L920)). The caller then raises a generic message ([extensions/fetch.py L299-L302](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/extensions/fetch.py#L299-L302)), and `fetch_plugin_with_resolution` re-wraps it as `PluginFetchError` ([fetch.py L132-L145](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/plugin/fetch.py#L132-L145)). 5. **Plugins cannot be edited after create.** `UpdateConversationRequest` has no `plugins` field ([models.py L613-L639](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/models.py#L613-L639)), and `LocalConversation` reads `_plugin_specs` only from its constructor ([L410-L416](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L410-L416)). 6. **Auto-load errors are emitted before the explicit loop.** Marketplaces are fetched, and `MarketplaceLoadError` is emitted, before the explicit plugins are fetched ([L1243-L1261](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L1243-L1261)). When the explicit plugin then raises, the whole method runs again on the next send and emits the event again. ## Reproduction This uses a real agent server started from source, plus `curl`. Nothing is mocked. The plugin source is a `file://` git URL to a bare repository that does not exist yet. Later the script creates that repository to show the retry. The plugin has one skill and one `UserPromptSubmit` hook that writes a marker file, so the script can check that the plugin really loaded. ```bash git clone https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk && cd software-agent-sdk git checkout 15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d uv sync --dev SDK=$PWD bash /path/to/repro.sh # script below; it kills only its own server PID ```
repro.sh ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Repro: explicit plugin fetch failure on first message -> raw HTTP 500. # Runs a real agent server from a source checkout. No mocks. # Usage: (cd software-agent-sdk && uv sync --dev && SDK=$PWD bash repro.sh) SDK=${SDK:-$PWD} PORT=${PORT:-18765} T=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$T/home" "$T/ws" "$T/remote" BASE="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api" PLUGIN_URL="file://$T/remote/sdk4-plugin.git" # does not exist yet # Plugin content: one skill and one UserPromptSubmit hook that writes a marker. P="$T/plugin-src" mkdir -p "$P/.plugin" "$P/skills/sdk4-skill" "$P/hooks" echo '{"name": "sdk4-plugin", "version": "1.0.0"}' > "$P/.plugin/plugin.json" printf -- '---\nname: sdk4-skill\ndescription: test skill\n---\nhello\n' \ > "$P/skills/sdk4-skill/SKILL.md" cat > "$P/hooks/hooks.json" <> $T/hook_marker"}]}]}} EOF # Real agent server, clean env, isolated HOME / persistence. cd "$SDK" env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$T/home" OPENHANDS_SUPPRESS_BANNER=1 \ OH_CONVERSATIONS_PATH="$T/convs" OH_BASH_EVENTS_DIR="$T/bash" \ "$SDK/.venv/bin/python" -m openhands.agent_server --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" \ > "$T/server.log" 2>&1 & SERVER_PID=$! trap "kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null; echo T=$T" EXIT for _ in $(seq 90); do curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" >/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done AGENT='{"kind":"Agent","llm":{"model":"gpt-4o","api_key":"dummy","usage_id":"agent"},"tools":[]}' MSG='{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"hello"}],"run":false}' new_conv() { # POST /conversations with the given JSON body; print the id curl -s -X POST "$BASE/conversations" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$1" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])' } user_msgs() { # number of user MessageEvents stored in the conversation curl -s "$BASE/conversations/$1/events/search?kind=MessageEvent&source=user" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)["items"]))' } send() { # POST a user message; print status and body curl -s -o "$T/out" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE/conversations/$1/events" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$MSG" echo " $(cat "$T/out")" } echo "== 1. Create a conversation with an explicit plugin whose source is missing" CID=$(new_conv "{\"agent\": $AGENT, \"workspace\": {\"working_dir\": \"$T/ws\"}, \"plugins\": [{\"source\": \"$PLUGIN_URL\"}]}") echo "conversation: $CID" echo "== 2. First message" send "$CID" echo "user messages stored: $(user_msgs "$CID")" echo "== 3. Resend while the source is still missing" send "$CID" echo "user messages stored: $(user_msgs "$CID")" echo "== 4. Make the plugin source exist (no API can edit plugins), then resend" git init -q --bare -b main "$T/remote/sdk4-plugin.git" git -C "$P" init -q -b main && git -C "$P" add -A \ && git -C "$P" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm init \ && git -C "$P" push -q "$T/remote/sdk4-plugin.git" main send "$CID" echo "user messages stored: $(user_msgs "$CID")" echo "hook marker lines: $(cat "$T/hook_marker" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)" python3 - "$T/convs/${CID//-/}/base_state.json" <<'PY' import json, sys s = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])) print("persisted skills:", [k["name"] for k in s["agent"]["agent_context"]["skills"]]) print("persisted user_prompt_submit hooks:", len((s.get("hook_config") or {}).get("user_prompt_submit", []))) PY echo "== 5. Create WITH initial_message and a missing plugin source" BEFORE=$(curl -s "$BASE/conversations/count") curl -s -o "$T/out" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$BASE/conversations" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{ \"agent\": $AGENT, \"workspace\": {\"working_dir\": \"$T/ws\"}, \"plugins\": [{\"source\": \"file://$T/remote/missing.git\"}], \"initial_message\": {\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"hi\"}]}}" echo " $(cat "$T/out")" echo "conversations on server: before=$BEFORE after=$(curl -s "$BASE/conversations/count")" echo "== 6. Auto-load marketplace that cannot be fetched (no explicit plugin)" AGENT_MKT="{\"kind\":\"Agent\",\"llm\":{\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"api_key\":\"dummy\",\"usage_id\":\"agent\"},\"tools\":[], \"agent_context\": {\"registered_marketplaces\": [{\"name\": \"broken-mkt\", \"source\": \"file://$T/remote/no-mkt.git\", \"auto_load\": true}]}}" CID2=$(new_conv "{\"agent\": $AGENT_MKT, \"workspace\": {\"working_dir\": \"$T/ws\"}}") send "$CID2" echo "user messages stored: $(user_msgs "$CID2")" echo "== 7. Broken auto-load marketplace AND broken explicit plugin: send twice" CID3=$(new_conv "{\"agent\": $AGENT_MKT, \"workspace\": {\"working_dir\": \"$T/ws\"}, \"plugins\": [{\"source\": \"file://$T/remote/missing2.git\"}]}") send "$CID3"; send "$CID3" curl -s "$BASE/conversations/$CID3/events/search?kind=ConversationErrorEvent" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("ConversationErrorEvent codes:", [e["code"] for e in json.load(sys.stdin)["items"]])' echo "user messages stored: $(user_msgs "$CID3")" echo "== server log" echo "'Unhandled exception on POST' lines: $(grep -c 'Unhandled exception on POST' "$T/server.log")" grep -m1 -o 'PluginFetchError: Failed to fetch plugin' "$T/server.log" ```
### Observed output ```text == 1. Create a conversation with an explicit plugin whose source is missing conversation: e6856c71-0d93-4c0c-b12e-84051dbfcff5 == 2. First message 500 {"detail":"Internal Server Error","exception":"Failed to fetch plugin from file:///tmp/tmp.aUv45YHEFu/remote/sdk4-plugin.git","error_id":"23bf302c9c8549f59ced73272d86a91d"} user messages stored: 0 == 3. Resend while the source is still missing 500 {"detail":"Internal Server Error","exception":"Failed to fetch plugin from file:///tmp/tmp.aUv45YHEFu/remote/sdk4-plugin.git","error_id":"2661c556e6b04ced8e156246d0f71ac7"} user messages stored: 0 == 4. Make the plugin source exist (no API can edit plugins), then resend 200 {"success":true} user messages stored: 1 hook marker lines: 1 persisted skills: ['sdk4-skill'] persisted user_prompt_submit hooks: 1 == 5. Create WITH initial_message and a missing plugin source 500 {"detail":"Internal Server Error","exception":"Failed to fetch plugin from file:///tmp/tmp.aUv45YHEFu/remote/missing.git","error_id":"000f1ffe591748c9a363deaaefe098c4"} conversations on server: before=1 after=2 == 6. Auto-load marketplace that cannot be fetched (no explicit plugin) 200 {"success":true} user messages stored: 1 == 7. Broken auto-load marketplace AND broken explicit plugin: send twice 500 {"detail":"Internal Server Error","exception":"Failed to fetch plugin from file:///tmp/tmp.aUv45YHEFu/remote/missing2.git","error_id":"1678084a5d804a01aaf9b64042a8ab13"} 500 {"detail":"Internal Server Error","exception":"Failed to fetch plugin from file:///tmp/tmp.aUv45YHEFu/remote/missing2.git","error_id":"e7331998d624443399d91843d79de0ac"} ConversationErrorEvent codes: ['MarketplaceLoadError', 'MarketplaceLoadError'] user messages stored: 0 == server log 'Unhandled exception on POST' lines: 5 PluginFetchError: Failed to fetch plugin T=/tmp/tmp.aUv45YHEFu ``` What the output shows: - Steps 2 and 3: the send fails with a raw 500, and no user message is stored, so a resend makes no duplicate. - Step 4: after the source exists, the resend returns 200. There is exactly 1 user message, the plugin hook fired, and the skill and hook are persisted. A retry works only because the *same* URL became valid. No API can point the conversation at a corrected URL. - Step 5: create with `initial_message` returns 500, but the conversation count went from 1 to 2. The client never received the new id. - Step 6: a broken auto-load marketplace on its own still degrades. The send returns 200 and the message is stored. - Step 7: two failed sends give two `MarketplaceLoadError` events, one for each attempt. ## Expected behaviour - An explicit plugin that cannot be fetched still blocks the conversation (no change to the #6439 contract). - The response is a mapped domain error, not a 500. It has a stable code, the redacted source, and a status that says what to do: fix the input (4xx) or retry (502/503). - A source string that cannot be parsed is rejected at create time with 422, as the install endpoints already do. - A failed initial message does not leave a conversation the client cannot see. - Retrying does not add duplicate auto-load error events. - The user has a supported way to fix a wrong plugin source, or the API documents clearly that they must start a new conversation. ## Proposed fix 1. **Map the error once at the domain level.** Make `PluginFetchError` also subclass `openhands.sdk.errors.UpstreamFailed` (502). Raise `Unprocessable` (422) for problems with the source itself: a source that cannot be parsed (`parse_extension_source`), an unsafe `repo_path`, a missing local path, or a plugin that fetched but failed `Plugin.load`. Adding a base class does not break existing `except PluginFetchError` callers. The existing `DomainError` handler ([api.py L799-L810](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/15bbd077d8a013fa0cf7554522b6c88e5171060d/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/api.py#L799-L810)) then maps the send, create and run paths with no change to the routes. Give the client a structured detail, for example `{"code": "PluginFetchError", "source": "", "message": ...}`, so a UI can name the plugin. 2. **Validate explicit plugin sources when the conversation is created.** Parse each `plugins[].source` in `start_conversation` and answer 422 before anything is persisted. 3. **Do not orphan the conversation on create.** When the initial message fails, either delete the just-created conversation before re-raising, or return the error with `conversation_id` in `DomainError.extra` so the client can recover or delete it. 4. **Emit auto-load errors once.** Collect the auto-load `ConversationErrorEvent`s while loading and emit them only after the explicit plugin loop succeeds. Or keep a per-instance set of codes that were already emitted. 5. **Separate transient from permanent fetch failures.** Keep the `GitCommandError` as the cause, as #7100 proposes. Then step 1 can choose 502/503 for network errors and 422 for "repository not found" or "ref not found". 6. *(Product decision, optional)* Allow `PATCH /api/conversations/{id}` to replace `plugins` while `_plugins_loaded` is still false. This lets a user fix a typo without losing the conversation. ## Proposed tests Put these in `tests/agent_server/` and use the real FastAPI app (`TestClient`). For the plugin source, use a `file://` bare repository under `tmp_path`, as in the repro. No mocks are needed. - A conversation with a missing explicit plugin: `POST /events` returns 502 (or 422, per step 1). The body has `code == "PluginFetchError"` and a redacted source. 0 user `MessageEvent`s are stored. - After the bare repository is created, the same `POST /events` returns 200. There is exactly 1 user `MessageEvent`, and `hook_config.user_prompt_submit` comes from the plugin. - `POST /api/conversations` with `plugins=[{"source": "not a source"}]` returns 422, and `/conversations/count` does not change. - `POST /api/conversations` with `initial_message` and a missing plugin returns a non-500 error, and it leaves no hidden conversation (or the response carries its id). - A broken auto-load marketplace plus a broken explicit plugin, sent twice: exactly 1 `MarketplaceLoadError` event. - A regression guard: a broken auto-load marketplace on its own still returns 200 on send. --- ## OpenHands AI triage **The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.** ### Triage Verified against `main` (and the pinned SHA in the reproduction): `PluginFetchError` is a plain `Exception` (`openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/plugin/fetch.py`), so a failed explicit-plugin fetch on `POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` falls through to the unhandled-exception 500 handler (`openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/api.py`); `_launch_prepared_conversation` persists the conversation and then sends `initial_message` with no rollback, so a failed initial message orphans it; auto-load `MarketplaceLoadError` events are emitted before the explicit-plugin loop and re-emitted on every retry because `_plugins_loaded` is only set after the whole load succeeds (`openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py`); `UpdateConversationRequest` has no `plugins` field. The repository has an authoritative mechanism that must be reused: the `openhands.sdk.errors` `DomainError` hierarchy, mapped to statuses once in `ERROR_STATUS` (`openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/errors.py`) and documented per route via `error_responses()`. Adjacent precedent already exists: `/api/plugins/fetch` maps strict plugin-source errors to 422/502/504 with a structured `{"code", "message"}` detail, and `/load_plugin` maps the same `PluginFetchError` to 400. The failing-closed contract for explicitly attached plugins (#6439) is unchanged by this issue. Bounded scope: map the explicit-plugin fetch failure to a domain error (502 `UpstreamFailed`, as proposed in the issue) on the send and create-with-`initial_message` paths; reject an unparseable `plugins[].source` at conversation create with 422 before persisting; ensure a failed initial message does not orphan the conversation (either nothing persisted, or the response identifies the conversation); emit auto-load error events only once per load attempt cycle so retries do not accumulate them; document the supported remediation for an attached plugin whose source fails (fix `${VAR}` secrets via `POST /{id}/secrets`, retry once the source is reachable, or start a new conversation) since `plugins` cannot be edited after create. Non-goals: no API to edit `plugins` after create (deferred product decision; document the workaround instead); no retry, caching, or git-error-classification changes to the auto-load marketplace path or to `try_cached_clone_or_update`'s error dropping — that is #7100's scope and is only coordinated here insofar as the 502 mapping must still work with the generic dropped-cause message; no change to the WebSocket send path, which already returns a `ServerErrorEvent` with `code="PluginFetchError"`; no change to `/load_plugin`'s existing 400 mapping; no change to the fail-closed behavior of explicit plugins. ### Acceptance Criteria - [ ] With an explicitly attached plugin whose source cannot be fetched (e.g. a `file://` bare repo that does not exist), `POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` returns HTTP 502 with a structured body whose code names `PluginFetchError` and whose source string is redacted (no credentials, no secret-expanded values), not a 500 `Internal Server Error` body, and the server does not log an unhandled exception for this path. - [ ] That failed send stores 0 user `MessageEvent`s, and a subsequent send retries the plugin load rather than being blocked (after the source becomes reachable, the send succeeds with exactly 1 user `MessageEvent` and the plugin's skills and hooks are loaded). - [ ] `POST /api/conversations` with a `plugins[].source` that `parse_extension_source` rejects (e.g. `"not a source"`) returns 422 before anything is persisted, and `/api/conversations/count` is unchanged. - [ ] `POST /api/conversations` with an `initial_message` and a failing explicit-plugin source returns the mapped domain error rather than a 500, and does not orphan the conversation: either no conversation is persisted (count unchanged) or the response lets the client identify the created conversation (e.g. a response field or header carrying its id). - [ ] With a broken auto-load marketplace and a broken explicit plugin, two consecutive failed sends produce exactly one `MarketplaceLoadError` `ConversationErrorEvent` total. - [ ] Regression guard: a broken auto-load marketplace with no explicit plugin still returns 200 on send and stores the user message (the #6439/#7100 degrade-open behavior is unchanged). - [ ] The send and create routes document the new error responses via the existing `error_responses()` mechanism; `/load_plugin`'s existing 400 mapping for `PluginFetchError` is unchanged, and existing `except PluginFetchError` callers (including the WebSocket path's `ServerErrorEvent`) behave as before. - [ ] The plugin/conversation API documentation states that `plugins` cannot be changed after create and names the supported remediations for a source that fails (fix `${VAR}` secrets via `POST /{id}/secrets`, retry once the source is reachable, or start a new conversation).
